decisionRationale.via: PR #792 draft-review instruction (launch-profile decision pass, following the ratified 40/40 requirement matrix)

notes.minorsIncluded: false for this cohort. Keeps School Beta's ratified rows correctly not-required for this beta; does not decide COPPA scope for later cohorts, which activate the same ratified rows without any matrix change.
notes.schoolManagedAccounts: false for this cohort. Same effect as minorsIncluded for the School Beta rows it jointly and independently gates. CLARIFIED 2026-08-16: this decision describes deployment/account-management scope, not participant employer affiliation. false means the initial beta is not yet a school-managed deployment - no student/minor accounts, no district-provisioned student roster, no district-owned/managed child accounts, no school-authorization legal basis for a minor, no production seat-reclaim/offboarding lifecycle, and no district rollout where an organization administers end-user accounts as a deployed service. It does NOT mean 'exclude participants employed by a school district.' Adult SLPs and teachers may participate using their own approved individual adult beta accounts even when their employer is a school district; only the deployment model - not the participant's job - is what stays out of scope. See cohortAdmissionBoundary below for the concrete list of actions that would cross into School Beta scope.
notes.mvpIncludesMinors: false. Pure Public MVP inheritance wiring (scripts/readiness-check.rb:722-726) - has zero effect on this beta's own card; deferred as a later, separate Public MVP scope decision.
notes.euUsersIncluded: false for this controlled beta cohort. This is a cohort-targeting/inclusion statement, not a technical access claim: it means EU participants are not part of the intended/approved beta cohort and the EU AI Act Art. 50 direct-interaction disclosure obligation is correctly treated as not-required for this cohort. It is NOT a representation that LingoLinq technically blocks EU users from reaching the service generally - no such block exists (verified: no geofencing/IP-country gate anywhere in app/ or lib/, confirmed by a targeted repo search turning up zero real hits).
notes.enforcementVerification: Before committing minorsIncluded=false / schoolManagedAccounts=false / euUsersIncluded=false, verified whether cohort exclusion is technically enforced at signup. Finding: it is NOT. api/users_controller.rb#create has no age/date-of-birth gate, no school-domain/org-type restriction, and no invite-code requirement (start_code is optional and only validated if present) - self-registration is open. No geofencing or IP-country blocking exists anywhere in app/ or lib/. The containment for this controlled beta is therefore OPERATIONAL (who Scot/the team actually invites and onboards), not a coded technical admission gate. This does not block applying the profile - the euUsersIncluded note above already anticipates a cohort-targeting rather than technical-block framing - but it means these three false values describe intended beta scope, not a system-enforced boundary, and should not be cited as a technical control in any compliance-facing claim without that caveat. Flagged as a candidate follow-up (a real admission gate: invite code, age question, or geographic scoping) if a technical backstop is later wanted; not built in this pass, which was a launch-profile decision review, not new engineering. CLARIFIED 2026-08-16: the operational admission control this needs to establish is narrower than 'no school affiliation' - it only needs to confirm a participant is an approved adult joining as an individual professional beta tester (their own account, their own capacity), regardless of who employs them. An SLP or teacher employed by a school district is in scope for this beta on that basis; requiring 'no school affiliation' would incorrectly exclude a large share of the intended adult professional cohort.
notes.cohortAdmissionBoundary: What Adult Beta participants (including SLPs/teachers employed by school districts) may do: use their own approved individual adult beta account to build boards, test AI board generation/word prediction/focus words, exercise accessibility workflows, and give professional feedback. What would cross into School Beta scope and must not happen until that milestone is intentionally activated (flag to Scot separately, do not just proceed): creating or using a real student account; entering identifiable student data as part of the beta; having a district provision or manage accounts (i.e. the organization administering end-user accounts as a deployed service, not an individual professional's own account); inviting students into the beta; or using LingoLinq as an actual district deployment. The practical line: participants may test the product themselves: they may not put an actual student into the system or use real identifiable student information as part of this beta.
notes.aiWordPredictionEnabled: true. Core AAC feature worth testing in the first beta. Its cache-scoping defect (LL-16ef84ad9a) has a real merged code fix (PR #788: ea40011ba 'scope the word prediction cache', 8cffa75c8 'salt the prediction cache'); the finding stays open only pending register reconciliation, not because the code risk is live. Enforced independently by the real server-side ai_word_prediction flag (lib/feature_flags.rb) plus org/user/COPPA/EU gates.
notes.aiFocusWordsEnabled: true. adult-beta-ai-focus-consent is claimed-done with zero open linked findings; the only gap is unrecorded runtime-verification evidence (paperwork, not a known defect). Enforced independently by its own real server-side flag plus the same gate family.
notes.aiBoardGenerationEnabled: true. Reversed from an initial draft recommendation to keep this off pending broader validation: Scot confirmed the actual first-beta SLP participants will specifically be testing AI board generation, making it a required feature for the intended test, not an optional surface-area expansion. Enforced independently by its own real server-side ai_board_generation flag plus the same org/user/COPPA/EU gate family verified for the other two AI features.
notes.silentPassGuard: This profile deliberately leaves adult-beta-ai-cache / adult-beta-ai-focus-consent / adult-beta-ai-master-consent in their honest done-awaiting-reconciliation / done-awaiting-verification states rather than forcing them to a clean 'done'. UPDATED 2026-08-16 (Codex correction pass, post-execution): a later execution pass DID record real evidence for the two ai-consent rows under evidence[id].code (RSpec-level code/test verification against real, unmocked production code) - that record is genuine and stays. But both requirements' verificationRequired is code-and-runtime, and no deployed-environment spot-check has occurred, so evidence[id].runtime is deliberately left absent rather than backfilled with a placeholder. scripts/readiness-check.rb now hard-fails any evidence[id] for a code-and-runtime requirement that isn't shaped as distinguishable {code, runtime} sub-objects, and claimed_done_substate only resolves 'done' when a runtime sub-object is actually present - so recording code-only evidence can never silently satisfy a code-and-runtime bar. Both rows correctly render done-awaiting-verification until a real deployed-beta spot-check happens and is recorded under evidence[id].runtime.

operationalControls.title: Controlled Adult / SLP / Teacher beta - minimum admission/participation control
operationalControls.note: This is a documented OPERATIONAL control (who Scot/the team actually invites, onboards, and permits to do what), not a technically enforced one. See decisionRationale.notes.enforcementVerification: api/users_controller.rb#create has no age/DOB gate, no school-domain restriction, and no invite-code requirement, and no geofencing exists anywhere in app/ or lib/. No DOB collection, geofencing, or new signup architecture has been added or is planned as part of this control - only if operational evidence later shows this process is insufficient (e.g. an actual out-of-scope admission occurs) would a technical backstop become worth considering.
operationalControls.via: PR #792 draft-review instruction (Codex-relayed operational-control pass, following the ratified 40/40 matrix and the launch-profile decisions)
requirements: Adult SLPs/teachers employed by school districts are allowed to participate.
Participation is in an individual professional beta-testing capacity, on the participant's own account - not a district-managed deployment.
No identifiable student data entered as part of the beta.
No inviting students into the beta.
No EU participants in the approved cohort.
Any request crossing these boundaries is escalated to Scot before proceeding, not resolved unilaterally.
operationalControls.relatedNotes: See decisionRationale.notes.schoolManagedAccounts and .cohortAdmissionBoundary for the fuller deployment-vs-employer-affiliation explanation behind items 2-3 and 4-7 above.

code.verifiedBy: Claude Sonnet 5 (PR #792 draft-review instruction, Codex-relayed execution pass)
code.method: Code/test verification ONLY - NOT a click-through of the actual deployed Cloud Run beta environment; this agent has no credentials or browser access to it. This is RSpec-level runtime execution of the real, unmocked production code against a real (local) Rails/Postgres instance: `DB_USER=scotw RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rspec spec/lib/feature_flags_ai_prefs_spec.rb spec/lib/feature_flags_spec.rb`, driving FeatureFlags.user_pref_allows_ai? and FeatureFlags.ai_feature_enabled_for? directly (not stubbed), covering: master preference nil/absent (grandfathered=allow), explicit false/0/'0' (deny), and specifically UNREADABLE/INVALID values ('', '   ', 'maybe', {}) denying rather than being grandfathered to allow - the exact 'unreadable or invalid master preference fails closed' claim this requirement makes. Also added and ran a new direct, unstubbed spec for the org-level ai_enabled_for? gate (previously only ever exercised via stubs across the whole suite), confirming the org disable_ai_features toggle independently blocks with no other gate state set.
code.result: 86/86 examples passing (81 pre-existing + 5 new). Fail-closed behavior on an unreadable/invalid master preference confirmed against real code, not assumed. This is code/test verification only; it does NOT satisfy this requirement's code-and-runtime bar by itself. A deployed-environment spot-check (corrupt/clear a real user's ai_features_enabled preference in the actual beta environment, confirm no AI output) is still required and has not yet occurred - record it under this entry's "runtime" key, not here, when it happens.
